lessons.name: TCP Socket Server from Scratch
lessons.desc: Raw socket(), bind(), listen(), accept() loop — handle multiple concurrent clients without a framework. Covers TCP handshake, partial reads, goroutine-per-connection, graceful shutdown.
lessons.q: Design a TCP echo server from raw POSIX sockets. Walk me through bind, listen, accept — and how you would handle 1000 concurrent clients without a framework.
lessons.qsub: TCP is a byte stream, not messages. How do you handle partial reads, and what happens when the client sends data faster than you read it?

lessons.name: HTTP/1.1 Server over Raw TCP
lessons.desc: Build HTTP/1.1 on raw TCP. Parse request line, headers, body via Content-Length. Route paths, serve responses, support keep-alive — zero stdlib http.
lessons.q: Build an HTTP/1.1 server on raw TCP sockets. How do you parse the request line, headers, and body? What does keep-alive actually do at the wire level?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding chunked? How do you handle a POST request with no Content-Length header?

lessons.name: DNS Resolver from Scratch
lessons.desc: Recursive DNS resolver: parse DNS packets, walk the hierarchy from root to authoritative, cache by TTL — raw UDP sockets and binary parsing.
lessons.q: Explain how a recursive DNS resolver walks from root servers down to authoritative answers. What does the DNS wire format look like?
lessons.qsub: Why does DNS default to UDP? When does TCP fallback happen, and how do you handle response truncation?

lessons.name: Event Loop from Scratch
lessons.desc: Single-threaded event loop using epoll/kqueue for I/O multiplexing. Timer min-heap for setTimeout semantics. Handle 1000 concurrent connections in one thread.
lessons.q: How does epoll work under the hood? Explain the difference between edge-triggered and level-triggered I/O notification.
lessons.qsub: Node.js handles thousands of connections on one thread. How does the event loop differ from a goroutine-per-connection model?

lessons.name: EventEmitter from Scratch
lessons.desc: on/emit/once/off, error event propagation, setMaxListeners, memory leak detection at 10+ listeners. The observer pattern backbone.
lessons.q: Build Node.js EventEmitter from scratch. How does once() auto-remove listeners, and why is the error event special?
lessons.qsub: Why warn at 10+ listeners on one event? How do you detect and fix memory leaks in evented systems?

lessons.name: Module Loader (require() from scratch)
lessons.desc: require() from scratch: resolution, __dirname, module.exports, caching, circular dependency handling with partial exports.
lessons.q: Rebuild Node.js require(). How does module resolution work, and how does caching prevent redundant loads?
lessons.qsub: Explain the circular dependency case: when A requires B which requires A, how does Node return partial exports?

lessons.name: In-Memory KV Store with File Persistence
lessons.desc: In-memory hash map + LRU eviction + append-only WAL for crash recovery. GET, SET, DEL, EXPIRE commands. Redis lite without the protocol.
lessons.q: Design an in-memory key-value store with WAL for crash recovery. What does the write-ahead log look like, and how do you replay it?
lessons.qsub: Explain LRU eviction — how do you get O(1) for both access and eviction? What is the trade-off with TTL-based lazy expiry?

lessons.name: TCP Connection Pool
lessons.desc: Pool of persistent TCP connections with borrow/return, health check, idle timeout, overflow strategy. Amortize handshake + TLS + auth cost.
lessons.q: Build a TCP connection pool. How do you handle borrow and return semantics, idle timeout, and health checks before lending?
lessons.qsub: What happens when the pool is exhausted? Compare blocking-with-timeout vs rejection vs queueing strategies.

lessons.name: WebSocket Server from Scratch
lessons.desc: HTTP upgrade handshake, WebSocket frame protocol, masking, fragmentation, ping/pong keepalive. Pub/sub broadcast across concurrent connections.
lessons.q: Walk me through the WebSocket upgrade handshake. How do you compute the Sec-WebSocket-Accept key from the client challenge?
lessons.qsub: Explain the WebSocket frame format — opcodes, masking, fragmentation. Why is client-to-server masking required by the spec?

lessons.name: Graceful Shutdown System
lessons.desc: Signal handling (SIGTERM/SIGINT), connection drain with timeout, health check flip 200→503, worker drain, force-kill fallback.
lessons.q: Design production-grade graceful shutdown. How do you drain in-flight requests without dropping connections?
lessons.qsub: Explain the health check flip from 200 to 503. How do load balancers discover the unhealthy instance and stop routing?

lessons.name: HTTP Server from Scratch (no Express)
lessons.desc: The foundation of Node.js — build a server using only the http module.
lessons.q: Build an HTTP server using only Node's built-in http module — GET /hello, POST /echo, 404 handling, JSON responses. Walk me through how you parse the request body from the incoming stream.
lessons.qsub: What happens if you forget res.end()? How would you guard against an oversized request body (DoS) and how do you know the body is complete?

lessons.name: CLI File Stats Tool
lessons.desc: Build a command-line tool using fs and process — tests Node fundamentals.
lessons.q: Build a CLI tool that takes a file path and prints line count, word count, character count, and the top 5 most frequent words. How do you handle a missing or unreadable file?
lessons.qsub: How would you make it stream-friendly so it can handle a multi-GB file without loading the whole thing into memory?

lessons.name: In-Memory TTL Cache
lessons.desc: A building block used in every Node.js service — caching with expiry.
lessons.q: Design an in-memory TTL cache with set/get/delete/clear and stats. Values expire after ttlMs — explain lazy expiry vs active expiry and when you would choose each.
lessons.qsub: What is the tradeoff of a background cleanup timer — how do you avoid running it too frequently while still evicting stale entries promptly?

lessons.name: Build a Logger with Log Levels
lessons.desc: Every Node.js app needs a logger — build one that writes to console and file.
lessons.q: Build a Logger class with debug/info/warn/error levels, colored console output, and newline-delimited JSON written to a file. How do you make the minimum level configurable at runtime?
lessons.qsub: Why newline-delimited JSON for the file format, and how would you make log writes atomic in a single process?

lessons.name: CSV Parser & Serializer
lessons.desc: Stream-friendly CSV parsing — tests string parsing and edge case handling.
lessons.q: Build parseCSV(text) and toCSV(records) that handle quoted fields, commas and newlines inside quotes, and escaped quotes. What is the naive approach and why does it fail?
lessons.qsub: Walk me through the state machine for quote tracking — what states exist and how do you detect an escaped quote ("")?

lessons.name: Config Loader (ENV + JSON + Defaults)
lessons.desc: Configuration management is a real production concern. Build it properly.
lessons.q: Build loadConfig() merging defaults → JSON file → env vars → runtime overrides, with nested keys (DB_HOST → config.db.host), type coercion, and required-field validation.
lessons.qsub: How do you deep-merge without mutating the defaults? What happens when an env var conflicts with the default value's type?

lessons.name: Recursive Directory Walker
lessons.desc: Build your own find command — tests async file system operations.
lessons.q: Build walk(dir, options) as an async generator that lazily yields file paths, with extension filters, maxDepth, and ignore patterns. How do you avoid infinite loops with symlinks?
lessons.qsub: Why an async generator instead of returning an array? How does backpressure apply to iterating a filesystem lazily?

lessons.name: Server-Sent Events (SSE) Endpoint
lessons.desc: Real-time data push without WebSockets — the simplest live-update mechanism.
lessons.q: Build an SSE endpoint at GET /events that pushes a counter every second, detects client disconnects, and supports Last-Event-ID resume. What headers and wire format are required?
lessons.qsub: What is the SSE message format (id/event/data/retry) and why send keepalive comments? When would you pick SSE over WebSockets?

lessons.name: Redis Clone (RESP + Commands + Persistence)
lessons.desc: RESP wire protocol, core commands (GET/SET/DEL/TTL/INCR/LPUSH), pub/sub fan-out, AOF + RDB persistence. redis-cli should connect and work.
lessons.q: Build a Redis-compatible server. How does the RESP wire protocol work, and how do you implement TTL with lazy expiry plus background sweep?
lessons.qsub: Compare AOF and RDB persistence. When would you choose each, and how do you handle fork-less RDB snapshots?

lessons.name: Message Queue with At-Least-Once Delivery
lessons.desc: Durable queue with producer/consumer, ack/nack, redelivery timer, dead-letter queue. At-least-once delivery via WAL + visibility timeout.
lessons.q: Design a message queue with at-least-once delivery. How does visibility timeout prevent duplicate processing?
lessons.qsub: Explain dead-letter queues. What makes a message "poison" and how do you isolate it without losing visibility?

lessons.name: HTTP Load Balancer
lessons.desc: Reverse proxy distributing traffic across backends. Round-robin + least-connections, active/passive health checks, connection draining, sticky sessions.
lessons.q: Build an HTTP load balancer. Compare round-robin and least-connections algorithms. How do health checks work?
lessons.qsub: How do you implement connection draining for zero-downtime backend deploys? What is the circuit breaker pattern?

lessons.name: Distributed Rate Limiter Service
lessons.desc: Standalone rate limiter: token bucket + sliding window + fixed window counter. Redis + Lua for atomic distributed counting. Rate limit headers.
lessons.q: Design a distributed rate limiter. Compare token bucket, sliding window, and fixed window counter algorithms.
lessons.qsub: Why is a Redis Lua script necessary for atomicity? What race condition does it prevent between check and decrement?

lessons.name: Distributed Cache with Consistent Hashing
lessons.desc: Consistent hash ring with virtual nodes, LRU eviction per node, cache-aside + write-through patterns. Client routes without central coordinator.
lessons.q: Design a distributed cache with consistent hashing. How do virtual nodes improve key distribution across nodes?
lessons.qsub: Explain the thundering herd problem on cache miss. How does singleflight deduplicate concurrent fetches for the same key?

lessons.name: Cron Job Scheduler Engine
lessons.desc: Cron expression parser, min-heap job queue, distributed lock (SETNX) for exactly-once execution, retry with exponential backoff.
lessons.q: Build a distributed cron scheduler. How do you parse cron expressions and compute the next run time?
lessons.qsub: How do you ensure exactly-once execution across multiple scheduler nodes? What happens when clocks drift between nodes?

lessons.name: RPC Framework (gRPC-lite)
lessons.desc: Protobuf-style wire format with varint + TLV encoding, TCP framing, unary + server-streaming, client stub generation from IDL.
lessons.q: Design a minimal RPC framework. How does varint encoding work, and why is length-prefix framing necessary over TCP?
lessons.qsub: Compare unary, server-streaming, and bidirectional streaming RPC. When would you choose each communication pattern?

lessons.name: Object Storage (S3-lite)
lessons.desc: HTTP API for PUT/GET/DELETE objects, bucket management, chunked upload, range requests (206), ETag validation, metadata index.
lessons.q: Build an object storage service. How does chunked upload work, and why are range requests important for large objects?
lessons.qsub: Explain ETag-based conditional requests. How do they prevent lost updates during concurrent uploads?

lessons.name: URL Shortener — Base62 encoding, collision handling, analytics
lessons.desc: Generate unique short codes using Base62 (a-z, A-Z, 0-9). Store mapping in DB (short_code → long_url). Handle collisions with retry. Add click analytics (IP, user-agent, timestamp). Use cache (Redis) for hot URLs. 301 vs 302 redirect.
lessons.q: How do you generate unique short codes for a URL shortener? How do you handle collisions?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between 301 and 302 redirects for URL shortening? How do you design the analytics pipeline?

lessons.name: Mini Express Router
lessons.desc: Understand how Express works by building it — middleware chain, params, error handling.
lessons.q: Build an Express-like framework: route registration with params (:id), middleware via app.use, next()/next(err), and a 4-argument error handler. How do you convert /users/:id into a matcher?
lessons.qsub: How does next(err) skip normal middleware and jump to error handlers? How do you distinguish a route handler from middleware?

lessons.name: Job Queue with Retry & Concurrency
lessons.desc: The backbone of background processing — build a production-grade job queue.
lessons.q: Design a JobQueue with configurable concurrency, retry with exponential backoff, status tracking, and lifecycle events. How does a job move through pending → active → completed/failed?
lessons.qsub: How do you prevent the same job being processed twice, and how does priority interact with retries?

lessons.name: API Rate Limiter Middleware
lessons.desc: Every production API has one — implement sliding window and token bucket.
lessons.q: Build Express rate-limiting middleware with fixed-window and sliding-window strategies, 429 responses with Retry-After, and rate-limit headers. How do you key by client?
lessons.qsub: What is the memory cost of sliding window per client vs fixed window, and how do you clean up stale entries to prevent leaks?

lessons.name: Stream-based File Processing Pipeline
lessons.desc: Node.js streams are heavily tested at senior level — build a real transform pipeline.
lessons.q: Build a streaming file processing pipeline: read a large CSV as a stream, parse, transform, filter, batch into groups of 100, and write JSONL — without loading the file into memory.
lessons.qsub: How do you handle a chunk that splits a line in half, and how does backpressure propagate through a chain of Transform streams?

lessons.name: Database Connection Pool
lessons.desc: Resource management pattern used in every production Node.js service.
lessons.q: Design a database ConnectionPool with acquire/release, min/max size, acquire timeout, idle timeout, and health checks. What happens when acquire exceeds max?
lessons.qsub: Why queue acquirers rather than erroring? How do you health-check a connection before handing it out and close idle ones?

lessons.name: Interactive CLI Tool (like Inquirer-lite)
lessons.desc: Build your own prompting library — tests raw TTY control and keyboard events.
lessons.q: Build a prompting library: text, password (masked), select via arrow keys, confirm, and checkbox — using raw-mode stdin. How do you detect arrow key presses?
lessons.qsub: Arrow keys arrive as multi-byte sequences — what do you actually receive in raw mode, and how do you re-render the menu in place?

lessons.name: File Watcher with Debounce
lessons.desc: Build your own chokidar-lite — recursive watching, change types, debouncing.
lessons.q: Build watch(dir, options) emitting add/change/delete events with debounce, recursion, ignore patterns, and an initial scan. How do you distinguish add from change?
lessons.qsub: fs.watch is unreliable across platforms — what fallback would you use, and how does debouncing prevent event floods?

lessons.name: WebSocket Handshake Server
lessons.desc: Implement the WebSocket upgrade handshake and basic framing from scratch.
lessons.q: Implement a raw WebSocket server: the HTTP upgrade handshake, Sec-WebSocket-Accept computation, and frame parsing/construction for text messages. Walk me through the accept-key computation.
lessons.qsub: Explain the frame header bits (FIN, opcode, mask, payload length) and why client-to-server masking is mandatory by the spec.

lessons.name: KV Store with AOF Persistence
lessons.desc: Redis-lite - a data store with append-only-file durability.
lessons.q: Design a KV store with AOF persistence: every mutation appends to a log, replay on restart, SAVE snapshots, TTL support, and keys() wildcard matching.
lessons.qsub: Why is append-only logging a good durability primitive? What happens if a log line is corrupt, and why truncate after a SAVE?

lessons.name: Webhook Delivery System
lessons.desc: Product companies run webhook infrastructure - retries, idempotency keys, and a delivery log.
lessons.q: Design a WebhookDispatcher with HMAC-signed delivery, per-attempt timeouts, exponential backoff retries, auto-disabling flaky endpoints, and a delivery log with replay.
lessons.qsub: How do you sign the body with X-Hub-Signature-256, and why HMAC rather than a plain hash? How does auto-disable interact with retries?

lessons.name: Idempotency Middleware
lessons.desc: Payments-grade APIs need idempotency - dedupe retried POSTs by key.
lessons.q: Build Express idempotency middleware: a client sends Idempotency-Key, duplicate keys return the stored response instead of re-executing, with a TTL and locking for concurrent duplicates.
lessons.qsub: How do you snapshot the response body before it is sent? How do concurrent duplicates share one result without a race?

lessons.name: Event Loop Scheduler (libuv-style)
lessons.desc: Rebuild libuv phases: timers → pending → poll → check → close. Microtask queue, nextTick priority, I/O starvation guard.
lessons.q: Rebuild the Node.js event loop phases. How do timers, I/O poll, setImmediate, and close callbacks interact?
lessons.qsub: Explain the priority order: process.nextTick, then Promise microtasks, then next phase. How can recursive nextTick starve I/O?

lessons.name: Stream Pipeline Engine
lessons.desc: Readable/Writable/Duplex/Transform with backpressure, highWaterMark, pipe(). Flowing vs paused mode, drain events.
lessons.q: Build Node.js streams from scratch. What is backpressure, and how does highWaterMark control data flow?
lessons.qsub: Compare flowing vs paused mode. How does pipe() chain streams with proper drain handling and error forwarding?

lessons.name: Cluster Process Manager
lessons.desc: Master forks workers, round-robin accept, IPC handle passing, worker health heartbeat, zero-downtime restart via SIGUSR2.
lessons.q: Rebuild Node.js cluster from scratch. How does round-robin accept distribute connections across workers?
lessons.qsub: Explain zero-downtime restart: fork new workers, drain old ones. How does IPC handle passing work across processes?

lessons.name: Worker Thread Pool
lessons.desc: Generic worker thread pool: task queue, thread lifecycle, SharedArrayBuffer for zero-copy, structured clone messaging, crash respawn.
lessons.q: Design a worker thread pool. How does SharedArrayBuffer enable zero-copy data sharing between threads?
lessons.qsub: Compare structured clone vs transferable objects. What is the right pool size for CPU-bound vs I/O-bound work?

lessons.name: Chat System — WebSocket, message persistence, presence, delivery receipts
lessons.desc: WebSocket for real-time messaging. Store messages in DB (PostgreSQL/MongoDB) with conversation_id, sender_id, content, timestamp. Presence service tracks online/offline status. Delivery receipts: sent → delivered → read. Message ordering with sequence numbers.
lessons.q: How do you design a chat system backend? How do you ensure message ordering and delivery?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between message queuing and real-time WebSocket delivery? How do you handle offline message delivery?

lessons.name: Notification System — fanout, multi-channel delivery, preferences
lessons.desc: Notification service with channels: email (SES/SendGrid), push (FCM/APNs), SMS (Twilio), in-app. User preferences per notification type. Fanout: single event → multiple channel delivery. Queue-based async processing. Delivery status tracking.
lessons.q: How do you design a notification system that supports multiple channels (email, push, SMS)?
lessons.qsub: How do you handle notification preferences? What is the fanout pattern and how do you prevent notification fatigue?

lessons.name: REST API with Auth, CRUD & Validation
lessons.desc: Build a full production-style API — the most common Node.js senior round problem.
lessons.q: Build a Notes REST API: JWT register/login, protected CRUD with ownership checks, request validation, and centralized error handling. How do you implement a JWT by hand?
lessons.qsub: Why HMAC-SHA256 for the signature and how does the server verify a token? What is the authorization check on PUT/DELETE?

lessons.name: CPU-bound Task with Worker Threads
lessons.desc: Offload heavy computation — tests your understanding of Node.js concurrency model.
lessons.q: Build a worker-thread pool that distributes CPU-bound tasks, handles worker crashes with requeue, supports cancellation, and reports progress. How does the main thread communicate with workers?
lessons.qsub: How do you detect a worker that crashed mid-task and requeue safely? Structured clone vs SharedArrayBuffer — when would you use each?

lessons.name: Pub/Sub Server with Channels
lessons.desc: Build the core of a message broker — think mini-Redis pub/sub over TCP.
lessons.q: Build a pub/sub server over TCP: SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH/UNSUBSCRIBE with wildcard channels and per-channel message history. How do you route a publish to matching subscribers?
lessons.qsub: How do you match news.* patterns, and how is a TCP stream framed into messages given partial reads?

lessons.name: Distributed Cache with TTL & LRU
lessons.desc: Combine everything: LRU eviction, TTL expiry, pub/sub invalidation, and HTTP API.
lessons.q: Design a CacheServer with an HTTP API combining LRU eviction and TTL expiry, an SSE endpoint for invalidation events, and a stats endpoint. How do LRU and TTL coexist?
lessons.qsub: How does a Map give you O(1) LRU eviction? Why an SSE endpoint for invalidation, and what metrics belong in /stats?

lessons.name: Cron-style Task Scheduler
lessons.desc: Build your own node-cron — parsing cron expressions and scheduling callbacks.
lessons.q: Build a cron-style Scheduler parsing expressions like */5 * * * * with ranges and lists, one-time tasks, cancellation, missed-run recovery, and a timezone option.
lessons.qsub: How do you compute the next run time by matching all five fields? What defines a missed run and how does the grace period work?

lessons.name: Streaming JSON Parser / Transformer
lessons.desc: Parse multi-GB JSON files without loading into memory — a real data engineering problem.
lessons.q: Build a streaming JSON parser as a Transform stream: JSONL lines or a streaming array, transform/filter each item, respect backpressure, and recover from malformed lines.
lessons.qsub: How do you buffer partial lines across chunks? What state machine parses a streaming array without waiting for the closing bracket?

lessons.name: Distributed Lock (SETNX-style)
lessons.desc: Cache stampede prevention, leader election, mutual exclusion - the lock everyone uses.
lessons.q: Design a DistributedLock with SET NX PX semantics, ownership tokens, compare-and-delete release, lease auto-renewal, and retry with backoff.
lessons.qsub: Why must release be compare-and-delete rather than GET-then-DEL? What happens when the lease expires mid-operation?

lessons.name: Worker Threads & Clustering — CPU-bound tasks in Node.js
lessons.desc: Worker Threads run JavaScript in parallel threads with shared memory. Cluster module forks Node.js processes across CPU cores.
lessons.q: Explain and build Node.js Worker Threads vs the cluster module: shared memory vs process forking, offloading CPU-bound work, and scaling HTTP servers across cores. When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between the libuv thread pool and Worker Threads? How does round-robin connection distribution work in cluster mode?

lessons.name: Caching Layer — Redis, cache-aside, cache invalidation strategies
lessons.desc: Redis caching layer for database query results, session data, and frequently accessed data.
lessons.q: Design a caching layer: cache-aside vs write-through, TTL and event-driven invalidation, cache stampede prevention with a distributed lock, and the Redis data structures you would use.
lessons.qsub: Why is delete-on-write sometimes better than update-on-write? How does SETNX prevent a thundering herd on cache miss?

lessons.name: AsyncLocalStorage Request Context
lessons.desc: Request-scoped state that survives async chains — request IDs, correlation IDs, tenant context.
lessons.q: Build a request-context helper using AsyncLocalStorage: assign a requestId (and optional userId/tenantId) per request, propagate it through every async call, and expose get()/set() helpers that any layer can read without passing arguments. How do you wire it into an Express-style middleware?
lessons.qsub: Why does ALS survive promises, timers, and stream callbacks when a plain closure would not? What are the memory risks of storing heavy objects in context?

lessons.name: Circuit Breaker with Fallback
lessons.desc: CLOSED → OPEN → HALF-OPEN state machine so a dead dependency fails fast instead of hanging requests.
lessons.q: Build a CircuitBreaker that wraps an async function: calls pass while CLOSED, failures increment a counter that trips the breaker OPEN after a threshold, OPEN fails fast (or returns a fallback), HALF-OPEN after a cooldown allows limited probe calls and closes on success. Emit state-change events.
lessons.qsub: How many probe calls should HALF-OPEN allow, and how do you prevent a thundering herd on recovery? When do you trip on 5xx but not 4xx, and how does the fallback get chosen?

lessons.name: Transactional Outbox Pattern
lessons.desc: Publish events reliably by writing to an outbox table in the same transaction as the business change.
lessons.q: Build the transactional outbox pattern: in one DB transaction, apply a business change AND insert a row into an outbox table; a relay polls committed outbox rows, publishes each to a queue (or HTTP endpoint), marks it sent, dedupes re-reads, and handles poison rows. Why is this more reliable than queueing inside the transaction?
lessons.qsub: What exactly fails when you enqueue inside the business transaction, and what does the relay do if the queue publish succeeds but marking sent fails?

lessons.name: Metrics Collector & /metrics Endpoint
lessons.desc: Prometheus-style counters, gauges, and histograms with a scrape endpoint — the observability staple.
lessons.q: Build a small metrics library: counters (monotonic), gauges (settable), histograms (buckets + sum + count), named with labels, exposed at GET /metrics in Prometheus text format, plus default process metrics (event-loop lag, memory, uptime) and per-route HTTP counters/latency.
lessons.qsub: Why histograms instead of average latency? How do you bound label cardinality, and why must counter rendering be atomic while iterating?

lessons.name: LSM-Tree KV Store (LevelDB-lite)
lessons.desc: MemTable (skip list) → SSTable flush, Bloom filter per SSTable, leveled compaction. The write path inside RocksDB and Cassandra.
lessons.q: Explain the LSM-tree architecture. How does the write path flow from MemTable to SSTable flush to disk?
lessons.qsub: What is write amplification in compaction, and how do Bloom filters reduce read amplification on the read path?

lessons.name: SQLite Clone (B-tree + WAL + SQL Parser)
lessons.desc: B+ tree page layout, WAL for ACID transactions, SQL lexer/parser/executor. File-backed relational DB with CREATE TABLE, INSERT, SELECT.
lessons.q: Design a file-backed relational database. How does B+ tree page layout work, and why are leaf nodes linked together?
lessons.qsub: Explain WAL for ACID atomicity. How does the page cache track dirty pages, and when does fsync happen on commit?

lessons.name: Git Clone (Object Store + DAG + Merge)
lessons.desc: Content-addressable object store, blob/tree/commit objects, pack files, three-way merge algorithm. Binary-compatible with real Git.
lessons.q: How does Git content-addressable object store work? What makes the Merkle DAG tamper-evident?
lessons.qsub: Explain the three-way merge algorithm. How do you find the common ancestor, and how are conflicts detected?

lessons.name: Programming Language Interpreter + Bytecode VM
lessons.desc: Lexer → recursive descent parser → AST → bytecode compiler → stack-based VM. Closures, mark-and-sweep GC, basic I/O.
lessons.q: Build a programming language interpreter. Walk through the pipeline: lexer, parser, bytecode compiler, and VM execution.
lessons.qsub: How do closures capture free variables via upvalues? Explain mark-and-sweep GC and why tri-color marking matters.

lessons.name: Raft Consensus Algorithm
lessons.desc: Leader election with randomized timeouts, log replication via AppendEntries, commit quorum, log compaction via snapshotting.
lessons.q: Explain the Raft consensus algorithm. How does leader election work, and what safety guarantees does it provide?
lessons.qsub: What is the log matching property? How does Raft ensure consistency after a network partition heals?

lessons.name: Container Runtime (namespaces + cgroups)
lessons.desc: Linux namespaces (PID/NET/MNT/UTS/IPC), cgroups v2 resource limits, OverlayFS layers, OCI-compatible create→start→kill→delete.
lessons.q: Build a minimal container runtime. What do Linux namespaces isolate, and how do cgroups enforce resource limits?
lessons.qsub: Explain OverlayFS union mounts. Why is pivot_root required instead of chroot for container security?
